source: A real attached session (`01a1f494-f08b-…`, cwd /private/tmp/unbien-capture, room J4PBgKbWsSGH) recorded by the web client itself: loaded with `?capture=1`, which tees every inbound envelope to `window.__unbienFrames`, then `__unbienDump("021-raw")` downloads it (web-client/src/app.ts). `raw.jsonl` is that dump — UNSCRUBBED, not committed: raw prompts, reasoning text, a pairing payload. `capture.py` turns it into the two committed inputs.
extensionVersion: @geohar/un-bien 0.25.15 (the build installed in this pi). The repo's extension source is at 0.25.11, and npm carries 0.25.13/14/15 that have no matching commits or tags in this repository — see vocab.md, 'Which build produced this', for why that does not invalidate the fixture.
scrub: capture.py, field-aware. Content fields (`text`, `thinking`, `summary`, `delta`, `errorMessage`) become LENGTH-PRESERVING `░` filler — deliberately, and only where length is small: past 2 000 characters a string becomes a `«length»` marker instead, because a 120 KB tool output repeated by every walk page would add 20 MB of block-shade characters that no comparison reads. A base64 image `data` payload is always `«length»` (it is counted, never compared). Every value under `details` is `«length»` at any length (a pairing token in a fixture is a credential in a repository); `sessionId` too, since it names a real room on a real relay. Any other string over the 48-char readable cap is filled. Entry ids, parentIds, toolCallIds, correlation ids, roles, tool names, mimeTypes, timestamps, stopReasons, usage numbers and sequence numbers are VERBATIM.
description: The vocabulary fixture. 020 proved a session's ordinary parts fold the same whether you watch them or load them; this one drives at the durable entry types NO scenario had ever fed through a page. A human drove one pi session (steps in `capture-steps.md`) while the client recorded: read an image, read a missing file, dump 120 KB of a HAR into context, `/compact`, branch the session and ACCEPT the branch summary, interrupt a long tool call with Esc. The session log ends with 187 entries: `session` header, 2 `model_change`, 1 `thinking_level_change`, 59 `custom` (the mempalace extension's state blob), 5 `custom_message`, 116 `message`, 1 `compaction` (2 122-char summary, `tokensBefore: 103812`, `firstKeptEntryId`), 1 `branch_summary` (2 853 chars, parented to an ANCESTOR of the old leaf, not to the leaf itself). `replay.jsonl` is one cold arrival: the 185-entry page plus the empty terminal page carrying leaf beacon `3d0107fa`.
pairing: Held to the same golden in both runners, and the two runs compared, with the exemptions vocab.md lists (`panels`/`subagents`/`pendingAsks` not persisted; `reasoning` rows live-only in both folds; the `hunks` block sidecar live-only). Two more are specific to this fixture and stated rather than filtered away: the SESSION TREE — branching means some entries sit on a branch the live run never watched, so the cold run legitimately holds rows the watching run does not; and `custom` entries (extension state, 59 of them) which NEITHER fold models, so neither renders them.
trims: Two reductions, both of OBSERVED redundancy, both recorded here because a fixture that quietly shrinks is a fixture nobody can audit. (1) WALK COLLAPSE: the client re-syncs on a 6-second timer, producing 81 walk runs / 136 pages that re-send the whole history — 12 MB of the raw capture. Kept: the FIRST walk and the FINAL walk. The final walk carries all 185 entries, so the live run still folds every entry, and first+final still exercises idempotence (rows keyed by live ids get re-keyed by a walk; a walk re-folded over rows that already exist). (2) DELTA TRIM: the session streamed 27 107 `message_update` frames (10 MB of prose). Deltas are kept for the 14 turns that carry this scenario's vocabulary (the image, the missing file, the big read, the compaction, the branch, the abort, and the last eight turns) and dropped for the other 37. NO other frame type is dropped: every `message_start`, `message_end`, `tool_execution_*` and `turn_*` frame survives, so every row is still birthed on the live plane, and every trimmed turn's entry still arrives through the final walk page.
note: Two findings this capture produced before any code ran, kept here so they are not re-derived. (1) OUT-OF-BAND EDITS REACH NOBODY: a `session_info` entry appended to the live session JSONL by hand sits in the file, is ignored by pi's own `getSessionName()` (it reads in-memory `fileEntries`, never re-read from disk), and is NEVER served by `get_entries` — so `session_info` is deliberately NOT pinned by this fixture; only a `/name` typed at the prompt produces one a viewer can see. Worth telling the owner: a running session is the only writer whose view of that file matters. (2) THE 6-SECOND RESYNC: the client re-walks whether or not anything changed, and the leaf beacon moved through 23 distinct ids during a ten-minute session. `capture.py` collapses that here, but the cadence is a live-plane fact. Not pinned: `session_info`, compaction of a COLD arrival (the compaction entry arrived while connected, and the client has never been tested against a session whose log was already compacted before attach).
